draft.title: Academic vocabulary
card: Academic texts, such as essays, reports and textbooks, use formal and precise words. They avoid casual words and slang.
Common academic words include analyse (examine closely), significant (important enough to matter), evidence (facts that support a claim) and consequently (as a result).
An academic word often replaces a vaguer everyday one. For example, "show" or "prove" may become "demonstrate", and "so" may become "consequently".
Precise words help a writer state a point clearly and sound serious. A reader can then see exactly what the writer means.
draft.remember: Academic words are formal and exact, so they say more clearly what you mean.

a.q: Which word is the most precise and formal way to say "look at closely" in an essay?
opts: Analyse
Check out
Glance at
Go over
a.why: Analyse means to examine something closely, and it suits formal writing. Check out is casual, and glance at means a quick look, which is the opposite of close.
a.clue: Which word sounds right in a formal essay?

b.q: Which sentence uses academic vocabulary correctly to show a result?
opts: The river flooded; consequently, the town closed its roads
The river flooded; evidence, the town closed its roads
The river flooded; analyse, the town closed its roads
The river flooded; significant, the town closed its roads
b.why: Consequently means as a result, so it links the flood to the closed roads. Evidence, analyse and significant are academic words too, but none of them can link a cause to its result in this way.
b.clue: Which word means as a result?

b.best: The river flooded; consequently, the town closed its roads

problems.detail: The question asks 'Which word', and Analyse is the only single-word option; the others are all phrasal verbs. A student could pick it from the wording alone, without knowing the idea.
